best_for: PC gamers with games spread across Steam, Epic, GOG, Battle.net and emulators who want one local library and launcher, and who are happy on Windows only.
description:
Playnite is a game library manager and launcher by Josef Nemec. Its own site, GitHub and Codeberg are the only official places to download it.

You can import games already installed on your PC without handing over any account details. Add-ons, installed from inside the app, bring new game stores, extra places to pull game info from, and new looks for both the desktop and fullscreen modes. Playnite tells you when a new version is out. If something goes wrong, the About menu builds a diagnostics package you can attach to a bug report. The project says the interface stays fast and light even with large libraries.

points.title: One library for every store
points.text: Playnite links your Steam, Epic, GOG, EA App, Battle.net, Ubisoft Connect and other accounts, and lists games you own even when they are not installed. Emulated console games sit in the same list.

points.title: Your library stays on your PC
points.text: The project says it keeps no user data on its servers. Library data is stored locally, and linking a store account saves only the session cookies or tokens a browser login would.

points.title: Free with nothing held back
points.text: Playnite is MIT-licensed open source and no features sit behind a paywall. The lead developer takes support through Patreon.

points.title: Couch mode and play time
points.text: A fullscreen mode works with a controller for TV setups, and Playnite tracks time played in every game, emulated ones included. Covers and descriptions come from IGDB automatically.

points.title: Extend it, theme it
points.text: Add-ons bring support for more game stores and full visual themes. You can write your own as .NET plugins or PowerShell scripts.

points.title: Windows only, and mid-rewrite
points.text: It needs Windows 10 or 11, with no Mac or Linux build. Most of the code is being rewritten for Playnite 11, so larger changes to version 10 are on hold.

points.title: Installer details
points.text: The installer listed here is 32-bit (x86) and installs for the current user, so no administrator rights are needed. A portable package is also offered. The Windows listing keeps 93 versions.
